chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Suleyman, from his uncle Abdullah ibn Hilal, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Take (pluck/cut) from your moustache and your nails every Friday. If there is nothing to take, then file them. Insanity will not befall you, nor leprosy, nor vitiligo.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling and benefit of trimming nails and moustache on Friday?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Friday ritual of grooming (fitrah) as a means of spiritual and physical purification, linking the removal of excess hair and nails to protection from specific ailments like insanity (junun), leprosy (jutham), and vitiligo (baras). In Shia scholarship, this practice is viewed not merely as hygiene but as a divine prescription that aligns the believer’s physical state with spiritual cleanliness, ensuring they remain free from both internal and external impurities throughout the week.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Suleyman, from his uncle Abdullah Bin Hilal who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Take (pluck) from your moustache and (cut) your nails during every Friday, so if there does not happen to be anything in these, so file it, and neither will insanity hit you, nor leprosy, nor vitiligo’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Sulayman from his uncle ‘Abd Allah ibn Hilal who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ’You must clip your mustache and fingernails every Friday, if you do not need clipping then just scratch them. You will not be affected by insanity, leprosy and albinism.’”
